column4: Visit note | 2026-01-15 03:30 PM | Dr. Sharmin Akter, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Taslima Sarkar, 27, female. Mrs. Sarkar explains that she keeps missing work or classes because of the pain and painful cramps she gets in the first days of each period. She works as a delivery rider, and her symptoms have felt worse since a job with long standing hours in Barishal. She denies fever, irregular bleeding, or unusual discharge. On examination: pain score 7/10, BP 124/82 mmHg, pulse 72 bpm, weight 70 kg. Abdominal and pelvic examination reveals tenderness without masses. Assessment: Primary dysmenorrhoea. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to use a hot water bottle, do light exercise, and keep a period diary. Follow-up in 3 months with the period diary.

Visit note | 2026-01-18 02:00 PM | Dr. Sharmin Akter, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Habiba Haque, 34, female. Mrs. Haque attends for review regarding her irregular periods and extra hair on the face. She works as a police constable and noticed weight gain after starting a desk job in Tongi. She reports taking her previous medications as directed and notes slight changes in her cycle length. On examination: BMI 28.8, BP 123/81 mmHg, pulse 75 bpm, weight 68 kg. Signs of mild hirsutism noted. Assessment: Polycystic ovary syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued to continue her management plan. She was advised to aim for 5% weight loss, exercise 150 minutes a week, and reduce sugary drinks. Follow-up in 3 months.
